parts.title: Why we love spicy food
paras: (0) Despite the pain it causes, chilli pepper is one of the most popular ingredients in the world. The burning [[1]] comes from a chemical called capsaicin, which tricks the brain into thinking that the mouth is actually hot.

So why do so many people actively [[2]] this unpleasant experience? One theory is that eating spicy food is a safe way of getting a thrill, a bit like [[3]] a roller coaster. The body reacts as if it were in danger, but the mind knows that there is nothing to worry [[4]].

Another explanation is cultural. In countries where chilli has been used for centuries, children are introduced to it gradually and soon [[5]] a taste for it. Interestingly, people who regularly eat spicy food become less [[6]] to the burning feeling over time.
Whatever the reason, chilli shows no [[7]] of losing its popularity. Some restaurants even hold competitions to see who can eat the hottest dish, although most doctors would [[8]] taking part.

q.expl: a burning sensation — жжение (физическое ощущение). Emotion и sentiment — чувства, impression — впечатление.
seek sth — искать, стремиться к чему-то (без предлога). Look, search и hunt требуют for.
ride a roller coaster — кататься на американских горках. Drive и steer — управлять машиной, sail — плыть.

acquire a taste for sth — постепенно полюбить что-то. Earn и win — заработать, выиграть; catch — поймать.

Устойчивое show no sign of doing sth — не проявлять никаких признаков.
discourage doing sth — не советовать, отговаривать. Dissuade и prevent требуют дополнения-человека (dissuade sb from), object — to.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Just keep walking
paras: Walking may be the simplest form of exercise there (0) is, but its benefits are surprisingly large. Regular walking strengthens the heart, helps to control weight and can even improve your mood. [[9]] is more, it costs nothing and requires no special equipment.

Many people believe that they need to walk [[10]] long distances to see any improvement, but this is not the case. Research suggests that walking briskly for just twenty minutes a day can make a real difference. The key is to walk fast enough to feel slightly out [[11]] breath.

To turn walking [[12]] a habit, experts suggest building it into your daily routine. You could get off the bus a stop early, take the stairs [[13]] of the lift, or go for a short walk after lunch. Walking with a friend can also help, because you are less likely to cancel if someone [[14]] is relying on you.
Best of [[15]], walking gives you time to think. Many famous writers and scientists claimed that their best ideas came to them [[16]] they were out walking.

q.expl: What is more — более того.
Усилитель перед прилагательным: very long distances.
out of breath — запыхавшийся.
turn sth into sth — превратить что-то во что-то.
instead of — вместо.
someone else — кто-то другой.
Best of all — а лучше всего.
while they were out walking — пока они гуляли.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Rainforests of the sea
paras: Coral reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, yet they are home to an (0) estimated quarter of all marine species. This incredible [[17]] has earned them the nickname 'rainforests of the sea'.

Unfortunately, reefs are [[18]] sensitive to changes in temperature. When the water becomes too warm, corals lose the tiny algae that give them their colour, a process known as [[19]]. If conditions do not improve, the [[20]] corals may die.

Scientists are working on several possible [[21]], including growing more heat-[[22]] corals in laboratories and planting them on threatened reefs. The long-term [[23]] of reefs, however, depends on slowing global warming, and each of us can help by making more [[24]] friendly choices.

q.expl: После This incredible нужно существительное: diversity — разнообразие.
Перед прилагательным sensitive нужно наречие: extremely.
coral bleaching — обесцвечивание кораллов; название процесса — форма на -ing.
the damaged corals — повреждённые кораллы; причастие в роли прилагательного.
После several possible нужно существительное во множественном числе: solutions.
heat-resistant — устойчивый к жаре; нужно прилагательное.
После The long-term нужно существительное: survival — выживание.
Перед прилагательным friendly нужно наречие: environmentally friendly — экологичный.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a teenage baker. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Rising early
parts.subtitle: Seventeen-year-old Callum Reid supplies bread to three cafés before he goes to school.
paras: Callum Reid gets up at four o'clock every morning, which is not something most seventeen-year-olds would choose to do. 'People assume I hate it,' he says, pulling a tray of loaves out of the oven, 'but the early hours are my favourite part. The town's asleep, the radio's on, and nobody's asking me anything.' By eight, the bread will be on its way to three local cafés, and Callum will be on his way to school.

It started with a school project on the science of fermentation. Callum's first attempts at sourdough were, in his own words, 'flat enough to use as doorstops'. Rather than giving up, he began keeping a notebook, recording the temperature of the kitchen, how long each dough rested and how the finished loaf turned out. 'I'm not naturally patient,' he admits. 'The notebook stopped me guessing. It made me see that every failure had a reason.'

The cafés found him, rather than the other way round. A neighbour who owns a small coffee shop tasted one of his loaves at a street party and asked if he could supply her every Saturday. Word spread quickly. Callum now bakes six days a week in a rented kitchen behind a pizza restaurant, which is empty in the mornings. 'The owner charges me almost nothing,' he says. 'I think he likes having the place smell of bread.'

Balancing the business with school is not easy. His parents agreed to let him carry on only if his grades did not suffer, and so far they haven't. 'It's made me much more organised,' he says. 'When you've only got an hour in the evening for homework, you don't waste it.' He does admit to falling asleep in the occasional afternoon lesson, though. 'My history teacher has been very understanding,' he grins.

Callum has been offered a place at a catering college next year, but he is not sure he will take it. 'Part of me wants to learn properly, from people who really know what they're doing,' he says. 'But another part of me is scared that if I go, someone else will take my customers.' For now, he is focusing on the next batch. The timer goes off, and he is already reaching for the oven door.

q.stem: What does Callum say about getting up early?
opts: He finds it harder than people realise.
He enjoys the peace it gives him.
He only does it because he has to.
He uses the time to plan his day.
q.hl: the early hours are my favourite part
q.expl: Ранние часы — его любимое время: город спит, никто ничего не спрашивает. Ловушка A: люди думают, что ему тяжело, а он говорит обратное.

q.stem: Why did Callum start keeping a notebook?
opts: His teacher asked him to record his results.
He wanted to understand why his bread went wrong.
He was planning to write a book about baking.
He found it hard to remember recipes.
q.hl: It made me see that every failure had a reason.
q.expl: Записи помогли перестать гадать и понять, почему каждая попытка не удалась. Школьный проект был началом, но вести блокнот учитель не просил.

opts: He persuaded local cafés to try his bread.
Someone who had tasted his bread asked him to supply it.
He won a baking competition at a street party.
A restaurant owner offered him a job.
q.hl: asked if he could supply her every Saturday
q.expl: «The cafés found him» — соседка попробовала хлеб и попросила поставлять ей. Ловушка D: владелец пиццерии сдаёт ему кухню, а не нанимает.

q.stem: What condition did Callum's parents set?
opts: He had to stop if he became too tired.
He had to keep up his school results.
He could only bake at weekends.
He had to save the money he earned.
q.hl: only if his grades did not suffer
q.expl: Родители разрешили, только если не пострадают оценки.

q.stem: What does Callum suggest about his history teacher?
opts: He has complained about Callum's behaviour.
He knows that Callum sometimes falls asleep in class.
He buys bread from Callum regularly.
He helps Callum to manage his time.
q.hl: My history teacher has been very understanding
q.expl: Он иногда засыпает на дневных уроках, а учитель истории «очень понимающий» — значит, знает и не ругает.

q.stem: How does Callum feel about the college place he has been offered?
opts: He is certain that he will accept it.
He thinks it would be a waste of time.
He has mixed feelings about it.
He is waiting for advice from his customers.
q.hl: Part of me wants to learn properly
q.expl: Одна часть его хочет учиться у профессионалов, другая боится потерять клиентов — смешанные чувства.

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a woman who opened a village bookshop. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Chapter one
parts.subtitle: Two years ago, Hannah Price gave up her office job to open a bookshop in a village of 800 people. Everyone said she was mad.
paras: When I told friends I was leaving my job in marketing to open a bookshop, most of them looked at me with pity. Bookshops, they reminded me, were closing all over the country. [[37]] But I had grown up in this village, and I knew how much people missed having somewhere to meet.

The building I found had been empty for years and needed a lot of work. [[38]] Neighbours turned up with paintbrushes, a local carpenter built the shelves for the cost of the wood, and the children from the primary school painted a sign for the door.

From the start, I knew I couldn't compete with online shops on price. [[39]] So I focused on the things they couldn't offer: personal recommendations, a comfortable armchair, and a cup of tea for anyone who wanted to sit and read for a while.

The events have turned out to be the most popular thing we do. Once a month, an author comes to talk about their work, and the shop is packed. [[40]] Last winter, we had to move one evening to the village hall because so many people wanted to come.
Financially, it has been a struggle. In the first year, I made less than half of what I used to earn. [[41]] Even so, I have never once regretted my decision.

What I love most is the conversations. Last week, an elderly man came in looking for a book he had read as a boy, but he couldn't remember the title or the author. [[42]] When he finally held it in his hands, he had tears in his eyes.

sents.B: I could never have afforded to do it all on my own.
sents.C: Most of my customers could get the same books cheaper with a single click.
sents.D: People often travel from other towns to be there.
sents.E: There were months when I seriously wondered whether I could keep going.
sents.F: It took us three days of searching, but we found it.
sents.G: My old boss even came in to buy a book.

q.expl: Книжные закрываются по всей стране → «They weren't wrong, of course» (A) → «But I had grown up in this village…» — уступка и возражение.
Здание требовало много работы → одна она бы не потянула (B) → пример помощи: соседи с кисточками, плотник, школьники.
Не может конкурировать по цене → покупатели могут купить дешевле одним кликом (C) → «So I focused on the things they couldn't offer».
Магазин битком → люди приезжают даже из других городов (D) → однажды пришлось переехать в сельский клуб.
Заработала вдвое меньше → были месяцы, когда она сомневалась, выдержит ли (E) → «Even so, I have never regretted».
Старик не помнил ни названия, ни автора → искали три дня, но нашли (F) → «When he finally held it…».

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four young people describe a skill they learned online. For questions 43–52, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: Learned online

texts.name: Marta
texts.body: My cousin was born deaf, and for years I relied on her parents to translate whenever we talked. When I was fifteen, I decided that wasn't good enough, so I started a free online course in sign language. The videos were excellent, but I soon realised that you can't learn a language from a screen alone. What really helped was practising with my cousin, who corrected me constantly and laughed at my mistakes. Now we chat for hours without anyone else's help, and she's even started teaching me the slang her friends use.

texts.name: Jonas
texts.body: I taught myself to code using free videos during a long summer holiday. At first, I just copied what the presenter did, without really understanding it. The turning point came when I tried to build a simple game of my own and nothing worked. Fixing it took me two weeks, but I learned more in those two weeks than in the previous two months. I've since built a website for my uncle's garage, which he says has brought him a lot of new customers. I still use online tutorials, but only when I'm stuck.

texts.name: Aiko
texts.body: Everyone laughs when I say I learned to knit from the internet, because they picture an old lady in a rocking chair. In fact, there's a huge community of young knitters online, and they're incredibly generous with their advice. I posted a photo of my first scarf, which was full of holes, and within an hour I had dozens of helpful comments. What surprised me most was how relaxing it is. Before exams, when I'm really anxious, knitting is the only thing that stops my mind racing.

texts.name: Ruben
texts.body: I've tried learning the guitar from online videos three times, and I've given up twice. The problem was that nobody was checking what I was doing, so I picked up some bad habits that were hard to break later. Third time round, I paid for a few lessons with a real teacher, who fixed my technique in weeks. Now I use a mix of both: the teacher once a month, and free videos for learning new songs. I don't think I'd have kept going without that combination.

q.expl: Марта годами общалась с глухой кузиной через переводчиков-родителей и решила выучить язык жестов.
